claims.statement: Polish guidance says URE may issue an efficiency certificate on the application of the project host or an authorised entity, and the resulting property rights are tradable on the energy exchange; the founder can seek pre-project authorization and a contractual share of certificate proceeds at the installer quotation gate, subject to counsel confirming aggregation and title.

KAPE states that ordinary certificates cover planned projects and the application must precede signing the contractor agreement and starting modernization, so an eligible project that signs too early can permanently lose support; URE reports nearly PLN 1.54bn of certificates issued for 2019-2023 efficiency investments, showing material monetisable value.

The ultimate buyer is an obligated electricity, heat, gas or fuel seller that must obtain and redeem certificates or pay a substitute fee, while the project owner can pay an intermediary from proceeds; KAPE publicly offers the full process on a success-fee basis, validating an outcome-funded service budget.

contrary_evidence: KAPE and other energy-audit specialists already offer end-to-end success-fee services, so the basic service is established and competitive.
Projects need audited savings and generally at least 10 toe of annual savings; many small installer jobs may be ineligible or not legally poolable.

economics.acquisition_route: Embed a one-page eligibility screen before the parents' company and partner installers issue a binding order; for passing projects, obtain authorization, order an independent audit and contract a share of the eventual tradable rights.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Prove ten projects through one installer, then embed with 50 installers sourcing 500 qualifying upgrades yearly; at PLN 8,000 average net fee the business reaches PLN 4m annual revenue, and retained cash plus a valued recurring installer network could plausibly produce PLN 5m founder net worth in 5-7 years.
economics.founder_time: Founder builds eligibility scoring and pipeline controls for 2-3 hours daily; accredited energy auditors and a brokerage partner handle audits and certificate sale.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Success fees must fund failed screens, audits and installer share; preliminary gross margin target is 35-55%, improving as eligibility prediction reduces wasted audits.
economics.payback: No upfront fee for the project owner; recover audit advances only from issued and sold rights, and require modeled proceeds at least three times external audit cost before accepting a case.
economics.pricing: 20-35% of net certificate proceeds after audit and exchange costs, shared with the referring installer; large projects may pay a smaller percentage with an audit deposit.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each installer quote is a new eligibility event; long-running installer embeds and standardized same-kind project data continuously refill the application pipeline.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Control at the pre-signature quote moment prevents eligibility destruction, while outcomes by upgrade type, auditor and URE decision improve acceptance scoring across installers.
fingerprint.customer: Polish SME energy users planning HVAC, insulation, motor, lighting, heat-pump or process-efficiency upgrades through regional installers.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A mandatory certificate-eligibility step embedded in installer CRM and quotation workflows before the customer signs.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Pre-project eligibility capture, authorised application, audit coordination and certificate sale funded by a share of realized proceeds.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The obligated energy-market buyer funds the certificate purchase; the project owner shares proceeds only after rights are issued and sold.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An installer is about to send a binding contract for an efficiency upgrade that could qualify only if filed first.

founder_fit: The parents' renewable-energy company offers immediate access to the exact pre-signature workflow where control must be acquired.
Eligibility classification, audit data and pipeline automation fit the founder's analytical and AI leverage.
Outcome funding limits client resistance and initial capital while auditors perform regulated technical work.
risks: An invalid filing sequence, audit or authorization can destroy certificate eligibility.
Certificate prices, URE processing times and sale liquidity can make payback slow or volatile.
Installer staff may bypass the eligibility gate under sales pressure, and incumbents can copy the integration.

structure.control_point: Pre-contract project authorization and economic rights captured inside the installer quote flow
structure.critical_dependency: URE eligibility, audit quality and lawful pooling or assignment of certificate proceeds

thesis: Own the few minutes before an efficiency order becomes binding: screen the upgrade, capture authorization before eligibility is destroyed, coordinate the audit and filing, then get paid only when tradable white-certificate rights are issued and sold.
title: Pre-Signature White-Certificate Capture
uncertainties: Counsel must confirm how same-kind small projects can be combined and how economic rights may be shared.
The qualifying rate and average certificate proceeds in the parents' and partner installers' pipelines are unknown.
Current URE processing duration and cash-conversion timing need direct validation.
